column1: # clues.tsv for ft_strrchr -- pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY listed case fails)
# The contract is man 3 strrchr (Libft, p.8: "adhering strictly to their definitions in the man page").
strrchr returns a pointer to the LAST occurrence of c. When c is there twice, which one is that, and what is returned when c is not there at all (man 3 strrchr, RETURN VALUE)?
The man page says the terminating null byte is "considered part of the string". So when c is 0, is there an occurrence to find, and where is it?
c is an int and the string holds chars: is a plain char signed on this machine? When the byte is 0xe9 and c is 233, are the two values you compare equal? Which conversion makes them so?
Is the occurrence you return the last one even when another sits at the very start, and when the only one does?
